faqs.question: What face paint can I do in under two minutes per child?
faqs.answer: A single cheek design in two or three colours: a candy-corn stripe, a googly eyeball, a potion bottle or a moon with a broom rider. Each needs one sponge press and a few brush strokes, which keeps a party queue moving at roughly 20 to 25 faces an hour by our estimate.

faqs.question: Is it okay to put face paint on the eyelids?
faqs.answer: Only if the label says its colours are approved for the eye area. Under US rule 21 CFR 70.5 a colour cleared for skin is not cleared for the eye area unless its listing says so, so most designs here stop about a finger-width outside the socket rim.

faqs.question: Is glow-in-the-dark face paint safe near the eyes?
faqs.answer: No. The glowing colour, luminescent zinc sulfide, is allowed in facial makeup at up to 10% for occasional use such as Halloween, but US rules require its label to say "Do not use in the area of the eye." Keep glow paint on the cheeks and jaw, and save it for adults.

faqs.question: Can I use kajal or surma for a black Halloween line?
faqs.answer: It's safer not to. The FDA says kohl is unapproved for cosmetic use in the US and has been linked to lead poisoning in children, and a 2025 study found some traditional eyeliners labelled lead-free with up to 610,000 ppm of lead. Use a cosmetic black that is approved for the eye area.

faqs.question: Is the face paint that comes in a toy makeup kit safe?
faqs.answer: Be cautious. A 2024 Istanbul study of 63 toy makeup products found 57 exceeded a limit for at least one toxic element, most often nickel. Buy face paint sold as a cosmetic with a full ingredient list instead.

faqs.question: Should every child get their own sponge?
faqs.answer: Yes, for anything near the eyes. The FDA warns against sharing or swapping eye cosmetics because another person's germs can cause infection, so cut a pack of sponges into wedges and give each child a fresh one.

faqs.question: When should I test a new face paint before the party?
faqs.answer: Give it 48 hours. Smear a little inside the forearm by 29 October and check it twice a day for redness or itching before you paint anyone's face.

faqs.question: My child's cheek went red after face painting. What now?
faqs.answer: Wash the paint off gently with lukewarm water and a mild soap, pat dry, and stop using that paint. If the redness persists or spreads near the eye, see a doctor, as the FDA advises for any eye cosmetic that irritates.

faqs.question: Which face paint designs suit someone with sensitive skin?
faqs.answer: The two-minute cheek designs, because they cover the least skin and stay away from the eyelids, which react more easily. Choose a fragrance-free paint, since fragrance is one of the common cosmetic allergens.

faqs.question: How do I show my kid's painted face to relatives who live far away?
faqs.answer: Put the photos in a one-person Halloween page and share the link; the /happy-halloween card fits six pictures and its Kids tone keeps everything cute rather than gory. Set the optional password before sharing, as 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators do.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Face Paint Ideas Timed at 2, 5 and 15 Minutes

The best Halloween face paint ideas match the time you have: a two-minute cheek design for a queue of kids, a five-minute design that frames the eyes without touching the lids, or a fifteen-minute full face. Below are 12 original designs, four per time block, each with skill level, colours and who it suits. Easy Halloween face paint needs only water-activated cakes, a sponge and one brush.

Two of our own numbers matter if you send the finished face to someone who missed it. 48.3% of SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, so a close-up beats a full-length shot, and 38.5% of creators password-protect a page before sharing, a habit worth copying for a child's photo. The safety rules come from US colour-additive regulations, FDA guidance and three peer-reviewed studies.

## What is Halloween face paint, and which type should you use?

Halloween face paint is a cosmetic that colours the skin of the face for a few hours, sold as water-activated cakes, creams or alcohol-activated palettes. In the US every colour in it must be approved for cosmetic use.

The rule most buyers miss concerns the eyes. Under [21 CFR 70.5, the federal rule on colour additives near the eye](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-70.5), a colour approved for skin is not approved for the eye area unless its listing specifically says so.

Water-activated cakes are the forgiving choice: they blend with a damp sponge and lift with soap and water. Creams survive sweat but smear fine lines. Craft acrylics, markers and poster paint are not cosmetics.

## 4 two-minute face paint designs for a queue of kids

Two minutes per face works out to roughly 20 to 25 faces an hour once you allow for rinsing brushes (our estimate, not a measured rate). Every design sits on one cheek or the back of a hand, so a child who dislikes paint near the eyes can still join in.

### 1. Candy-corn cheek stripe

2 minutes, skill 1 of 3, yellow, orange and white, ages 3 and up. Sponge a thumb-sized yellow triangle onto the cheekbone, press orange into the middle third and white into the tip. Leave the edges soft; a crisp outline adds a minute nobody notices.

### 2. Googly eyeball

2 minutes, skill 1 of 3, white, green or blue, and black, ages 4 and up. Paint a coin-sized white circle, a coloured iris slightly off-centre, then a black pupil. One white dot on the pupil makes it look wet, and the off-centre iris makes it glance sideways.

### 3. Bubbling potion bottle

2 minutes, skill 2 of 3, purple, green and white, ages 5 and up. Brush a round-bottomed purple flask, dab the lower half green, then flick three white bubbles out of the neck. Angle the bottle so the bubbles drift towards the temple, away from the eye.

### 4. Moon and broom

2 minutes, skill 2 of 3, yellow and black, ages 6 and up or adults in plain black. Sponge a yellow crescent on the upper cheek and cross it with a tiny black rider in four strokes: a handle line, a bristle fan, a triangle hat and a dot for the head.

## 4 five-minute designs around the eyes, without painting the lids

These frame the eyes, so the 21 CFR 70.5 rule applies to all four. Keep paint on the brow bone, temple and cheekbone, about a finger-width outside the bony rim of the socket. The FDA's [eye cosmetic safety page](https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/cosmetic-products/eye-cosmetic-safety) warns against sharing eye products, so give each child a fresh sponge wedge.

### 5. Owl brow feathers

5 minutes, skill 2 of 3, brown, white and orange, ages 4 and up. Sponge brown across both brows, paint three rows of small white U-shaped feathers climbing upward, then an orange beak triangle on the bridge of the nose, kept above the nostrils.

### 6. Raven wing sweep

5 minutes, skill 2 of 3, black, deep blue and silver, teens and adults. Brush five black teardrop feathers fanning from the outer corner of each eye to the temple, starting at the socket edge rather than the lid. Drag blue through each feather and add a silver centre line for sheen.

### 7. Haunted skyline brow

5 minutes, skill 2 of 3, purple, black and yellow, ages 7 and up. Sponge a purple dusk band across the forehead, then paint black rooftops, a crooked tower and a picket fence along the top of the eyebrows. Two yellow square windows make it read as houses in a photo.

### 8. Three-eyed monster

5 minutes, skill 1 of 3, green, white and black, ages 3 and up. Sponge green over the forehead and brows, add a third eye mid-forehead using the googly-eyeball method from design 2, then draw spiky black eyebrows just above the real ones.

## 4 fifteen-minute full-face designs

Full faces cover the most skin, so patch-test these first and remove them most gently. Fifteen minutes assumes a clean, dry face and paint laid out; add five for a wriggly child.

### 9. Patchwork scarecrow

15 minutes, skill 2 of 3, tan, orange, brown and yellow, ages 5 and up. Sponge tan over the face, add orange and brown square patches on opposite cheeks and a triangle nose, then flick yellow straw strokes from the hairline and jaw. On deeper skin tones, layer the tan twice so it dries even.

### 10. Peeking mummy

15 minutes, skill 2 of 3, off-white, grey and black, ages 6 and up. Paint diagonal off-white bands two fingers wide, leaving the area around one eye bare as the gap the mummy peers through. Shade one edge of each band grey and line the gap in black.

### 11. Medusa coils

15 minutes, skill 3 of 3, sage, gold and dark green, teens and adults. Sponge sage over face and neck, then paint two or three snakes rising from the jaw and curling past the temples, each with a dark spine and gold highlight. Their heads point outward at the hairline, clear of the eyes.

### 12. Glow night sky (adults only)

15 minutes, skill 3 of 3, navy, black and glow yellow-green. Sponge navy over half the face and scatter stars and two constellations from chin to temple. Under [21 CFR 73.2995 on luminescent zinc sulfide](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-73.2995), the glowing colour may be at most 10% of a facial makeup meant for occasions such as Halloween, labelled "Do not use in the area of the eye." Keep it on cheek and jaw.

## Which face paint design fits your time, age and skin?

The table groups the 12 designs by time block. Read the eye-area column first if anyone has sensitive skin.

| Time block | Designs | Youngest age | Colours | Eye-area exposure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 minutes | 1–4 | 3 | 2–3 | None: cheek or hand |
| 5 minutes | 5–8 | 3 | 3 | Close: brow, temple, cheekbone |
| 15 minutes | 9–11 | 5 | 3–4 | Full face, lids left bare |
| 15 minutes, glow | 12 | Adults | 3 | Kept off the eye area by law |

Painting ten children? Stay in the first row: ten 15-minute faces take 150 minutes.

## Patch testing, the eye area, sensitive skin and removal

Patch-test every new paint two days ahead: a fingertip smear inside the forearm, left on as long as the costume will be, then watched for redness, itching or bumps for 48 hours. Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027, so test by the 29th either year.

Reactions are not rare. A 2026 review in [Acta Dermato-Venereologica on adverse effects of cosmetics](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13294297) puts cosmetic contact dermatitis at about 1–5% of the general population and notes that thinner eyelid skin reacts more easily. Roughly 80% of contact dermatitis is irritant rather than allergic, so harsh scrubbing does as much damage as paint.

The same review lists fragrance, preservatives and metals among common triggers. For sensitive skin, pick a fragrance-free paint, stay with the two-minute cheek designs, and repeat a borderline patch test.

Toy makeup carries its own risk. When Istanbul researchers analysed [63 toy makeup products bought from local stores](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11136717), 57 (90.48%) exceeded a limit for at least one toxic element, nickel most often. Buy paint sold as a cosmetic with a full ingredient list.

Do not use kajal or surma to deepen a black line. The FDA page above says kohl is unapproved for cosmetic use in the US and has been linked to lead poisoning in children. A [2025 King County, Washington study of traditional eyeliners](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12193921) found some labelled lead-free holding up to 610,000 ppm of lead, against an FDA guideline of 10 ppm.

Remove paint the same night. Water-activated paint lifts with lukewarm water and mild soap; creams and glow paints come away faster after a cleansing balm. Work from the edges inward, eyes closed near the brow, and pat dry. If irritation persists, the FDA advises stopping the product and seeing a doctor.

## Sharing the painted face, and when to skip the paint

Paint lasts one evening; the photo survives. If a grandparent or a friend abroad missed it, the [interactive Halloween card with up to six photos](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is a five-minute build in which the recipient carves a jack-o'-lantern and clears misted portraits to reveal your photos. Choose its Kids tone and the ghosts turn round and blushing, with nothing gory.

The [premium Halloween page with a 60-second voice note](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) is a ten-minute build with room for a dozen photos, one per painted sibling or cousin, and when it is made for kids the No button is never shown. For other occasions, the [full SubhSandesh template gallery](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) has the rest.

A SubhSandesh page draws 11.1 views on average, so a painted-face photo will be looked at more than once, another reason to set the optional password on a child's page. Each one greets a single person; neither works as a party invitation.

Skip the paint for a child with eczema, a cut or a rash on the face, or anyone who reacted to the patch test; a hat carries the costume instead. Skip our pages for someone who rarely uses a phone: a printed photo beats a link, and the pages are English-only.

## Sources

- 21 CFR 70.5, eCFR (undated current text)
- 21 CFR 73.2995, eCFR (added 8 August 2000)
- FDA, Eye Cosmetic Safety (current as of 28 June 2022)
- Yu & Schalock, Acta Dermato-Venereologica (24 June 2026)
- Mercan et al., Environ Sci Pollut Res (2 May 2024)
- Mokashi et al., PLOS Global Public Health (25 June 2025)

sources.stat: 21 CFR 70.5(a): no listing or certification of a colour additive authorises its use in the area of the eye unless the listing specifically provides for that use; such use otherwise counts as an unlisted colour additive. Current eCFR text read; no publication date.

21 CFR 73.2995: luminescent zinc sulfide may colour externally applied facial makeup at no more than 10% by weight, for limited infrequent occasions e.g. Halloween; label must state 'Do not use in the area of the eye.' Source: 65 FR 48377, 8 Aug 2000. Current eCFR text read.

Do not share or swap eye cosmetics; kohl (kajal, surma) is unapproved for cosmetic use in the US, consists of heavy-metal salts such as lead and antimony and has been linked to lead poisoning in children; if an eye cosmetic causes irritation stop using it and see a doctor if it persists. No publication date; content current as of 2022-06-28.

Yu & Schalock, Acta Derm Venereol 2026 narrative review: contact dermatitis from cosmetics affects about 1–5% of the general population; irritant contact dermatitis is ~80% of contact dermatitis; eyelids are particularly susceptible (thinner stratum corneum); common haptens include fragrance, preservatives, surfactants, metals. Full text read; CC BY-NC, cited and linked only.

Mercan et al., Environ Sci Pollut Res 2024 (Istanbul University-Cerrahpasa): 63 toy makeup products from local stores; 57 of 63 (90.48%) exceeded limits for at least one toxic element, in descending order Ni > Cr > Co > Pb > Sb > Cd > As > Hg. Full text read, CC BY 4.0.

Mokashi et al., PLOS Glob Public Health 2025: some traditional eyeliners labelled 'lead-free' contained up to 610,000 ppm lead, well above the FDA guideline of 10 ppm; traditional eyeliners had median 10 ppm lead vs 0.06 ppm for nontraditional. Full text read, CC BY.
